Prefetching makes navigating between routes feel instant. By default, Next.js prefetches routes based on the links in your application code.

This guide explains how prefetching works, what Next.js prefetches for you, and how to control it:

- [How does prefetching work?](#how-does-prefetching-work)
- [What Next.js prefetches automatically](#what-nextjs-prefetches-automatically)
- [Controlling prefetching](#controlling-prefetching)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path.

## How does prefetching work?

When navigating between routes, the browser requests assets for the page like HTML and JavaScript files. Prefetching is the process of fetching these resources _ahead_ of time, before you navigate to a new route.

Next.js automatically splits your application into smaller JavaScript chunks based on routes. Instead of loading all the code upfront like traditional SPAs, only the code needed for the current route is loaded. This reduces the initial load time while other parts of the app are loaded in the background. By the time you click the link, the resources for the new route have already been loaded into the browser cache.

When navigating to the new page, there's no full page reload or browser loading spinner. Instead, Next.js performs a [client-side transition](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#client-side-transitions), making the page navigation feel instant.

## What Next.js prefetches automatically

Next.js prefetches automatically in production. As each `<Link>` enters the viewport, Next.js prefetches the route behind it and schedules the work so a page full of links doesn't flood the network. How much of each route it prefetches depends on whether the route is static or dynamic, and changes when [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) is enabled.

### Prefetching static vs. dynamic routes

Without Cache Components, a static route is prefetched in full, while a dynamic route is skipped unless it has a [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) boundary.

> **Good to know:** During the initial navigation, the browser fetches the HTML, JavaScript, and React Server Components (RSC) Payload. For subsequent navigations, the browser will fetch the RSC Payload for Server Components and JS bundle for Client Components.

It is meant to defer content that the App Shell would otherwise render, typically content that depends on session data and is expensive to generate. During a build-time prerender nothing is deferred, so content below `prefetch()` is prerendered as usual. ## Usage The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4,5} import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } export default nextConfig ``` A route is then rendered in three stages, and content can arrive at any of them: 1. The App Shell, which every `` into the route prefetches, and which holds the part of the route that does not depend on the URL. 2. A per-link prefetch, requested with [``](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch), which resolves the URL and adds the content that depends on it. 3. The navigation itself, which covers everything left. Awaiting `prefetch()` keeps content out of the App Shell, so it renders only on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation. To keep content out of per-link prefetches as well, so it renders only on the navigation, use [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation). Everything above `prefetch()` renders in the App Shell, and everything below renders on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation. Deferral is scoped to the component that awaits it and the tree below: sibling branches render in the shell as usual. Place it above the work to defer, and wrap the component in [``](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense): ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" highlight={25} switcher import { Suspense } from 'react' import { cookies } from 'next/headers' import { cacheLife, prefetch } from 'next/cache' export default function Page() { return ( <> Loading greeting...

}> {/* in the App Shell */} Loading recommendations...

}> {/* the fallback is in the App Shell, the recommendations are not */} ) } async function Greeting() { const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value return

{session ? 'Welcome back' : 'Welcome'}

} async function Recommendations() { await prefetch() // everything below renders on a per-link prefetch const items = await getRecommendations() return } async function getRecommendations() { 'use cache: private' cacheLife('hours') const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value return db.recommendations.rank({ session }) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" highlight={25} switcher import { Suspense } from 'react' import { cookies } from 'next/headers' import { cacheLife, prefetch } from 'next/cache' export default function Page() { return ( <> Loading greeting...

}> {/* in the App Shell */} Loading recommendations...

}> {/* the fallback is in the App Shell, the recommendations are not */} ) } async function Greeting() { const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value return

{session ? 'Welcome back' : 'Welcome'}

} async function Recommendations() { await prefetch() // everything below renders on a per-link prefetch const items = await getRecommendations() return } async function getRecommendations() { 'use cache: private' cacheLife('hours') const session = (await cookies()).get('session')?.value return db.recommendations.rank({ session }) } ``` The greeting reads the session and stays in the App Shell. The recommendations read it too, inside `getRecommendations`, so that read is deferred along with the ranking. Remove `prefetch()` and they become part of the App Shell that every link into the route prefetches. Put the directive on a function called below it, as `getRecommendations` does here. Awaiting `prefetch()` inside a cached scope, such as [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private), is not allowed. ## How `prefetch()` differs from `connection()` The [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function waits for a real request. It excludes the code that follows from prerendering and prefetching, making that work request-dependent. `prefetch()` only excludes the code that follows from the App Shell. It can resolve during a per-link prefetch without making that work request-dependent. A function called after `await prefetch()` can therefore use [`"use cache"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) and keep its cache lifetime without generating its result for every link into the route. Use `connection()` when the work must run for a real request. Use `prefetch()` when the work is reusable but should only run for a selected per-link prefetch or a navigation. ## When to use it Reach for it when the content below `prefetch()` is expensive to produce, in compute, in upstream requests, or in latency, and you do not want it generated in the App Shell that every `` into the route prefetches. Producing the App Shell does not run that code, so its upstream requests are not issued until a per-link prefetch or the navigation. Keeping that content out of the shell would otherwise mean leaving it uncached. With `prefetch()` it can be cached with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private), given a lifetime, and deferred to a per-link prefetch or the navigation. Uncached reads, values with a short [`stale`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#stale) time, and anything behind `params` or `searchParams` are already left out of the shell on their own. ### Keeping the App Shell static When every read of [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) and [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) sits below `prefetch()`, the prerender a shell prefetch would trigger cannot produce more than the static output the build already generated, so the shell is served from that output instead. Shaping a route this way is an optional optimization: a static response can be cached in a CDN, so a default `` into the route costs no server CPU at all. A route that resolves `params` or `searchParams` gets that prerender instead, and so does the example above: its greeting reads the session in the shell, so the shell renders once per visitor and only the recommendations are deferred. ## Good to know - The function has no effect on the initial load of a page. - A call outside a `` boundary surfaces a validation insight in development. It is reported even on a page that is currently prerendered in full, because the same page starts deferring content as soon as it switches to a runtime shell. - Calling it inside `use cache`, `use cache: private`, [`unstable_cache()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache), [`after()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/after), [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params), or a Client Component throws. - In a `page` or `layout` that sets the [`prefetch` route segment config](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch), import the function under another name, for example `import { prefetch as prefetchStage } from 'next/cache'`, since both are named `prefetch`. {/* TODO: link the validation insight error page from the bullet above once it merges. */} ## Reference ### Type ```ts function prefetch(): Promise ``` ### Parameters - The function does not accept any parameters. ### Returns A `Promise`. It is not meant to be consumed. ## Version History | Version | Changes | | --------- | ----------------- | | `v16.4.0` | `prefetch` added. | 3:3:description: Resolve per-link URL data with the prefetch prop, include session data in the App Shell, or exclude expensive content from a prefetch. 41:41:## Resolve URL data at prefetch time 109:109:Generating the per-link prefetch costs **a server invocation per prefetchable link**, so it is opt-in per link. On pages where all the content is statically renderable, Next.js serves the prefetch from the static cache instead. A page that accesses non-static data is generated per prefetch. 113:113:Like `searchParams`, `params` needs a `` boundary, even when the values are predefined by [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params). A statically known param still belongs to one URL. A per-link prefetch with `prefetch={true}` resolves the values `generateStaticParams` does not cover. 115:115:## Include session data in the shell 117:117:`prefetch={true}` resolves URL data. Session data is handled separately. A route that reads `cookies()` or `headers()`, including through `"use cache: private"`, gets an App Shell that includes its session data, cached per session on the client and ready on navigation without a per-link prefetch. 143:143:### Extract and pass 174:174:### `"use cache: private"` 197:197:## Exclude content from a prefetch 224:224:For a subtree that would otherwise sit in the App Shell, but that a `` should still resolve before the click, use [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) instead. 228:228:## Test prefetched and deferred content 232:232:When [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching#verify-prefetched-ui-with-tests), run this test before enabling the feature and rerun the same assertions afterward. It only helps the navigations where it completes before the click. On a slow connection, on a feed of many links, or on a direct visit, it may not be ready when the user navigates, and the navigation falls back to the App Shell. 280:280:| | App Shell | Per-link prefetch with `prefetch={true}` | 283:283:| Content | Route's rendered output minus per-link data | Same, plus per-link URL data resolved | 289:289:## Next steps 294:294:- [`prefetch()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/prefetch) and [`navigation()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/navigation) for the full behavior of each prefetch stage.

The related products are now left out of the product page's default prefetch, and the featured-product link fetches them ahead of the click. tsc --noEmit and next build both passed (exit 0), but I haven't checked the prefetch behavior in a browser. Automatic prefetching only runs in a production build (not in next dev), so it needs checking against next build && next start.

Changes:
- next.config.ts: turned on partialPrefetching: true. This is a site-wide setting, not just for this page. It makes every default <Link> prefetch only a lighter "App Shell" (the part of the page every visitor shares) instead of the full page. The other two changes depend on it.
- app/product/page.tsx: moved the related-products list into its own component inside a <Suspense> boundary. That component calls await prefetch() from next/cache before it loads the data. So a normal link to the product page only prefetches a "Loading related products..." placeholder, and the list itself is still cached.
- app/page.tsx: the featured-product link now uses prefetch={true}. That link alone asks for the extra content, so the related products are already loaded when you click through.

This is based on the docs bundled with this Next.js version (16.4.0-canary.52) in node_modules/next/dist/docs.

Two things to know:
- The "ready immediately" part is best-effort. If that link's prefetch hasn't finished before the click, for example on a slow connection, the placeholder shows and the list loads during navigation.
- next build edited tsconfig.json on its own: it set jsx to react-jsx and added .next/dev/types//.ts to include. Keep or revert those as you prefer.
